section_summary: This section covers U.S. State Department correspondence and intelligence from January through April 1938 concerning Japanese finances, war budgets, and international borrowing efforts. It features numerous protests from American citizens, civic organizations, and Chinese groups against proposed commercial credits and loans to Japan, alongside internal State and Treasury Department discussions on restricting bank credits for aircraft and munitions exports under the Neutrality Act. Additionally, it contains detailed analyses of Japanese foreign exchange reserves, regular reports on gold bullion shipments to the United States, and official reporting on Japan's general and China Incident budgets.

subfiles.about: Inquiry whether a favorable consideration of a Japanese loan could promote world stability.
subfiles.summary: Baker asks if the United States might aid world stability by favorably considering a Japanese loan.
subfiles.title: Letter from S. J. Baker to Department of State

subfiles.about: State Department acknowledgment that it is unaware of proposed American loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton replies that the Department is unaware of any proposed loans to Japan by American interests.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to S. J. Baker

subfiles.about: Protest urging the President to prevent a fifty-million-dollar credit to Japan for Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Thompson urges President Roosevelt to block a reported credit to Japan, enclosing a letter from a missionary.
subfiles.title: Letter from May Bel Thompson to President Roosevelt

subfiles.about: Eyewitness account of Japanese bombing of Chinese cities and aggressive regional expansion.
subfiles.summary: A missionary doctor recounts devastating Japanese air raids on Soochow, Changchow, and Wusih, warning of wider conquest.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Letter from Missionary Doctor in China
subfiles.to: Friends and Sharers in the work of the Kingdom

subfiles.about: State Department reply acknowledging receipt of a missionary letter referred from the White House.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges Thompson's letter and enclosed missionary report forwarded from the White House.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to May Bel Thompson

subfiles.about: Analysis of Japanese gold holdings, production, foreign securities, and bank balances abroad.
subfiles.summary: This memorandum reviews Commercial Attaché Williams' report on Japan's foreign exchange resources, adjusting estimates of gold reserves to forty million dollars. It evaluates the illiquidity of Japanese-held foreign securities and estimates overseas bank balances.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japan's Foreign Exchange Resources

subfiles.about: Confidential report that Swiss National Bank rejected Japanese loan feelers.
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports that Swiss National Bank officials are definitely unfavorable toward Japanese loan inquiries.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7 from Bern

subfiles.about: Department distribution sheet for Bern telegram No. 7.
subfiles.summary: State Department distribution list routing telegram No. 7 from Bern to senior officers.
subfiles.title: Distribution Slip for Telegram No. 7 from Bern

subfiles.about: Summary excerpt of telegram No. 7 from Bern.
subfiles.summary: Summary extract regarding Harrison's report on Swiss National Bank's unfavorable attitude to Japanese loan feelers.
subfiles.title: Summary of Telegram No. 7 from Bern

subfiles.about: Transmittal of copies of telegram No. 7 from Bern to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal slip sending six copies of Bern telegram No. 7 to the Secretary of the Treasury.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Slip to Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Transmittal of paraphrase of telegram No. 3 to Bern to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal slip sending six copies of telegram No. 3 paraphrase to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Slip to Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Instructions thanking Harrison and requesting continued reporting on financial matters for Treasury.
subfiles.summary: Telegram relaying Treasury's thanks to Harrison and requesting continued reporting on loan and financial developments.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 3 to American Legation Bern

subfiles.about: Protest against American corporate or private financial loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Monroe registers a strong protest against any American loans to Japan, urging application of the Neutrality Act.
subfiles.title: Letter from Paul Monroe to Stanley K. Hornbeck

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of Monroe's protest against financial loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck acknowledges receipt of Monroe's protest and states it will be brought to senior departmental attention.
subfiles.title: Letter from Stanley K. Hornbeck to Paul Monroe

subfiles.about: Treasury note expressing appreciation for Harrison's cable from Bern.
subfiles.summary: Treasury letter requesting compliments and thanks be conveyed to Minister Harrison in Bern.
subfiles.title: Letter from Treasury Department to Herbert Feis

subfiles.about: Protest against American loans to Japan as harmful to China.
subfiles.summary: Chamberlain warns that American loans to Japan would provide material assistance and moral backing against China.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph P. Chamberlain to Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department acknowledgment of Chamberlain's letter opposing loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges Chamberlain's letter expressing opposition to American financial loans to Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to Joseph P. Chamberlain

subfiles.about: Appeal urging the State Department to prohibit loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Crane urges Hull to stop American loans to Japan, arguing foreign financial aid strengthens the military caste.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mrs. W. Murray Crane to Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department acknowledgment of Mrs. Crane's views on loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges Crane's letter regarding the extension of loans to Japan by American financial interests.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to Mrs. W. Murray Crane

subfiles.about: Protest by Detroit citizens against a contemplated fifty-million-dollar loan to Japanese industrialists.
subfiles.summary: The committee protests a fifty-million-dollar industrial loan to Japan, citing war atrocities and demanding aid for China.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Committee to Aid Chinese People to Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Resolution requesting the State Department discourage loans for the development of Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The association requests Hull discourage loans to Japanese agents for Manchukuo's industrial development.
subfiles.title: Letter from Inter-Professional Association to Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Department acknowledgment of the Inter-Professional Association's resolution.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges Barry's letter conveying the resolution against lending money for the development of Manchukuo.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to John D. Barry

subfiles.about: Record of discussions with Gordon Rentschler on bank credits for exports and rumors of a Chinese loan.
subfiles.summary: Green discusses National City Bank's credits for airplane sales to Japan and Rentschler's denial of Chinese loan rumors.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Gordon S. Rentschler

subfiles.about: Recommendation to closely question Rentschler regarding commercial credits for airplane exports.
subfiles.summary: Feis advises questioning Rentschler further and discouraging bank credits for aircraft and engine sales to Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Herbert Feis on Airplane Export Credits

subfiles.about: Argument for querying National City Bank regarding war material financing to Japan under the Neutrality Act.
subfiles.summary: Feis proposes two specific questions to Rentschler regarding munitions financing and the potential application of the Neutrality Act.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Herbert Feis on Arms Financing

subfiles.about: Review of proposed policy toward bank credits and direct restrictions on arms exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Green reviews Feis's proposals concerning Rentschler and asks the Secretary whether to discourage credits or study direct arms export controls.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Joseph C. Green for Secretary Hull

subfiles.about: Report on Japanese loan inquiries in Switzerland and a silver-backed Swiss credit to China.
subfiles.summary: Bern reports that the Swiss National Bank rejected Japanese loan approaches, while Swiss Bank Corporation granted China a silver-backed credit.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 221 from Bern

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Despatch No. 221 from Bern to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal note enclosing copy of Bern Despatch No. 221 on Swiss loan inquiries for the Treasury.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Slip to Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Request for State Department intervention regarding missing Imperial Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Siegelstein requests diplomatic aid to resolve an impasse with Yokohama Specie Bank over replacement of lost Japanese sterling bonds.
subfiles.title: Letter from Bennett E. Siegelstein to Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: State Department refusal to intervene in a private legal controversy over replacement bonds.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth declines diplomatic action, stating the bond dispute is private and subject to determination by judicial tribunals.
subfiles.title: Letter from Green H. Hackworth to Bennett E. Siegelstein

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note regarding Japanese pamphlets on war resources and finance.
subfiles.summary: Document file note cross-referencing Tokyo Despatch No. 2768 enclosing pamphlets on Japan's conflict and financial resources.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Tokyo Despatch No. 2768

subfiles.about: Report of a fifteen-million-yen gold shipment from Japan to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Bank of Japan advice that fifteen million yen in gold was shipped to the United States on February 26.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 142 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Paraphrase text of Tokyo telegram No. 142 on gold shipment.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of telegram No. 142 regarding the Bank of Japan's fifteen-million-yen gold shipment.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 142 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmittal of paraphrase of telegram No. 142 from Tokyo to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal note enclosing six copies of the paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 142 for the Treasury.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Slip to Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note regarding Japan's balance of payments with Manchukuo for 1935 and 1936.
subfiles.summary: Document file note cross-referencing Mukden tables showing Japan's balance of payments with Manchukuo as a losing proposition.
subfiles.title: Document File Note on Mukden Despatch

subfiles.about: Diplomatic transmission of Chinese civic petition against industrial credits to Japan for Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Johnson transmits a petition from Chinese civic leaders urging the United States to block credits for Manchurian heavy industry.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4 from Hankow

subfiles.about: Chinese civic appeal to discourage American credit for the Manchuria Heavy Industry Development Company.
subfiles.from: People's Foreign Relations Association of China
subfiles.summary: Chinese organizations appeal to Ambassador Johnson to discourage American credit negotiations reportedly initiated through Thomas J. Watson.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Petition from Chinese Civic Organizations

subfiles.about: Military intelligence report on Japan's general and China Incident budgets and bond issues.
subfiles.summary: Military attaché report analyzing Japan's 1938-39 budget, special China Incident appropriations, and national bond issuance.
subfiles.title: MID Report No. 9220 on Japanese Government Budgets

subfiles.about: Confidential notification of three upcoming Japanese gold shipments to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports three gold shipments scheduled via Kinkwa Maru, Komaki Maru, and Titibu Maru totaling seventy million yen.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 211 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 211 regarding gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrased text of telegram No. 211 detailing three Japanese gold shipments to the United States.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 211 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Distribution routing sheet for Tokyo telegram No. 211.
subfiles.summary: State Department routing slip distributing copies of Tokyo telegram No. 211 to department officers.
subfiles.title: Distribution Slip for Telegram No. 211 from Tokyo

subfiles.about: Summary note of scheduled Japanese gold shipments reported in telegram No. 211.
subfiles.summary: Brief summary note detailing the three scheduled gold shipments on the Kinkwa Maru, Komaki Maru, and Titibu Maru.
subfiles.title: Summary Note on Gold Shipments

subfiles.about: Transmittal of paraphrase of Tokyo telegram No. 211 to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal slip enclosing paraphrase copies of Tokyo telegram No. 211 for the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Slip to Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Notice from the Treasury regarding three Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Internal memorandum conveying Lochhead's telephone notice that Japan is shipping three six-million-dollar gold consignments.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Treasury Notice of Gold Shipments

subfiles.about: Detailed report on the promulgated Japanese general budget for fiscal year 1938-1939.
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits a comprehensive analysis of the promulgated 1938-1939 general budget balanced at 2.87 billion yen. It includes detailed statistical breakdowns of departmental expenditures, ordinary tax receipts, government monopoly revenues, and extraordinary deficit bond issues.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2819 on Japanese Budget 1938-1939

subfiles.about: Report on Diet approval of a supplementary budget for the China Incident.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Diet approval of a 4.85-billion-yen supplementary budget for the China Incident, enclosing a press clipping.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2826 on China Incident Budget

subfiles.about: Press clipping reporting Diet presentation of supplementary fighting estimates and tax increases.
subfiles.summary: Newspaper clipping reporting Lower House examination of the 4.85-billion-yen fighting estimates, bond authorizations, and provisional tax revisions.
subfiles.title: Enclosure: Fighting Estimates Presented to Diet

subfiles.about: Protest by American citizens in Shanghai against rumored cotton loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: American residents in Shanghai urge President Roosevelt to reject proposed loans or cotton credits to Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Americans in Shanghai to President Roosevelt
